preamble: Under the laryngeal theory, the Proto-Indo-European laryngeal *h₂ became the vowel a when it stood between consonants (or after a consonant word-initially) and so had to carry the syllable: *ph₂tḗr 'father' > Greek πατήρ, Latin pater, Proto-Germanic *fadēr, Proto-Celtic *ɸatīr, whereas Indo-Iranian has i (Sanskrit pitár-). This vocalization is distinct from laryngeal colouring, in which *h₂ next to *e turned the vowel into a and was itself lost; colouring does not belong in this cell. The atlas symbol [h] stands in for *h₂, whose phonetic value is reconstructed as a pharyngeal [ħ], velar [x] or uvular fricative rather than a glottal [h]. Greek alone keeps the three laryngeals apart (h₁ > e, h₂ > a, h₃ > o); Latin, Germanic and Celtic give a from all three.

examples.note: Zero grade of *steh₂- 'stand'; contrast θετός (*dʰh₁tós, e) and δοτός (*dh₃tós, o), the Greek triple reflex.
Cognate of Greek στατός and Sanskrit sthitá- (with i).
Via Proto-Germanic *fadēr (earlier *faþḗr); also Old English fæder, Old Norse faðir.
Via Proto-Celtic *ɸatīr, with loss of initial *p.
